extracted.intended_audience: Members of the public and stakeholders submitting comments on EPA pesticide tolerance proposals (e.g., registrants, growers, importers, NGOs, researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal/technical standards governing EPA proposed tolerances for pesticide residues and the public notice-and-comment process for EPA pesticide tolerance rulemakings (registration review actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting CBI
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit CBI to EPA through email or https://www.regulations.gov. If you wish to include CBI in your comment, follow the applicable instructions at https://www.epa.gov/dockets/commenting-epa-dockets#rules and clearly mark the information that you claim to be CBI. Information so marked will not be disclosed except in accordance with procedures set forth in 40 CFR part 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow EPA’s docket-specific instructions for CBI submissions (do not use regs.gov or email for CBI); clearly mark claimed CBI; disclosure governed by 40 CFR part 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tips for preparing comments
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing and submitting your comments, see the commenting tips at https://www.epa.gov/dockets/commenting-epa-dockets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use EPA’s published commenting tips (linked) for practical advice on formatting, content, supporting evidence, and how to submit via the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment period length (FFDCA §408(e)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to issuing the final regulation, FFDCA section 408(e)(2) requires EPA to issue a notice of proposed rulemaking for a 60-day public comment period, unless the Administrator for good cause finds that it would be in the public interest to have a shorter period and states the reasons in the proposed rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comments within the 60-day window unless the rule states a different, justified shorter period; EPA must state reasons if comment period shortened for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process to retain a tolerance proposed for revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule provides a 60-day public comment period that allows any person to state an interest in retaining a tolerance proposed for revocation. If EPA receives such a comment within the 60-day period, EPA will not proceed to revoke the tolerance immediately. However, EPA will take steps to ensure the submission of any needed supporting data and will issue an order in the Federal Register under FFDCA section 408(f), if needed. If the data are not submitted as required in the order, EPA will take appropriate action under FFDCA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To request retention, file a timely comment stating interest and be prepared to provide supporting data if EPA issues an order under 408(f). After final rule publication, you may file an objection or request a hearing within the time specified; failing to file an objection within that time waives rights to raise issues resolved in the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and legal consequence of a tolerance
rubrics_metrics.description: A “tolerance” represents the maximum level for residues of a pesticide chemical legally allowed in or on food, which includes raw agricultural commodities and processed foods and feed for animals. Under the FFDCA, residues of a pesticide chemical that are not covered by a tolerance or exemption from the requirement of a tolerance are considered unsafe. Foods containing unsafe residues are deemed adulterated and may not be distributed in interstate commerce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication: food-use pesticides sold/distributed in the U.S. must have appropriate tolerances/exemptions and registration under FIFRA; imported commodities treated with pesticides must have U.S. tolerances or exemptions to enter commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration and harmonization with Codex and other international MRLs
rubrics_metrics.description: When establishing a tolerance for residues of a pesticide, EPA must determine whether Codex has established a MRL for that pesticide. Additionally, as part of the registration review of a pesticide EPA determines whether Codex or other international MRLs exist for commodities and chemicals for which U.S. tolerances have been established. Where appropriate, EPA’s intention is to harmonize U.S. tolerances with those international MRLs to facilitate trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harmonization considerations are summarized in the tolerance reassessment section of the chemical-specific Human Health Draft Risk Assessments; EPA may modify U.S. tolerances to align with Codex, Japanese, or other international MRLs when supported by data and trade facilitation goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration review obligations (FIFRA §3(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under FIFRA section 3(g), EPA is required to periodically review all registered pesticides and determine if those pesticides continue to meet the standard for registration under FIFRA. As part of registration review of a pesticide, EPA also evaluates whether existing tolerances are safe, whether any changes to existing tolerances are necessary or appropriate, and whether any new tolerances are necessary to cover residues from registered pesticides. Any tolerance changes identified during registration review are summarized in registration review decision documents (PID, PFD, ID, FD) and placed in the public docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders can find supporting registration review risk assessments and decision documents in the public docket at https://www.regulations.gov using the docket ID listed in the rule; registration review is an explicit occasion for tolerance reassessment and regulatory updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety standard for establishing/modifying/revoking tolerances (FFDCA §408)
rubrics_metrics.description: FFDCA section 408(b) authorizes EPA to establish a tolerance if the Agency determines that a tolerance is safe; the FFDCA defines 'safe' to mean that 'there is a reasonable certainty that no harm will result from aggregate exposure to the pesticide chemical residue, including all anticipated dietary exposures and all other exposures for which there is reliable information.' This includes exposure through drinking water and in residential settings but does not include occupational exposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must base tolerance decisions on aggregate exposure/risk assessments; special consideration must be given to infants and children per FFDCA section 408(b)(2)(C), and EPA must consider factors listed in 408(b)(2)(D). Documentation of these considerations appears in chemical-specific risk assessments and registration review documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for a practical method to detect/measure residues (FFDCA §§408(b)(3) & (c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: When establishing tolerances or exemptions from the requirement of a tolerance, FFDCA sections 408(b)(3) and (c)(3) require that there be a practical method for detecting and measuring pesticide chemical residue levels in or on food, unless in the case of exemptions EPA determines that such method is not needed and states the reasons therefore in the rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tolerance actions must be accompanied by adequate enforcement methodology described in supporting documents; if exemption claimed, EPA must state reasons why a practical method is not needed in the rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: OECD rounding and tolerance-expression practices
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule reflects the Agency’s 2019 adoption of the Organization of Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) Rounding Class Practice. All tolerance values proposed in the regulatory text of this rulemaking, modified or otherwise, are being proposed to reflect current OECD rounding practices (e.g., removing trailing zeros, rounding to the nearest tenth decimal where appropriate). More information on the OECD Rounding Class Practice can be found at https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/mrl-calculator-users-guide-and-white-paper_9789264221567-en.html.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will modify tolerance numeric expressions (remove trailing zeros, round as appropriate) to conform with OECD practices; these changes are intended to be non-substantive to the permissible level of residues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crop group updates and conforming pre-existing crop groups (40 CFR 180.40(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: 40 CFR 180.40(j) states that 'At appropriate times, EPA will amend tolerances for crop groups that have been superseded by revised crop groups to conform the pre-existing crop group to the revised crop group.' EPA has indicated in updates that registration review is one such appropriate time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will update commodity/crop group definitions and establish or remove individual commodity tolerances to avoid redundancy when revised crop group definitions supersede prior groupings; stakeholders should review proposed group changes and resulting additions/removals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed effective and expiration dates policy for tolerance reductions/revocations
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is proposing that these tolerance actions would be effective on the date of publication of the final rule in the Federal Register. For actions in the final rule that lower or revoke existing tolerances, EPA is proposing to add an expiration date to the existing tolerance that is six months after the date of publication of the final rule in the Federal Register, to allow a reasonable interval for producers in exporting members of the World Trade Organization’s Sanitary and Phytosanitary Measures Agreement to adapt to the requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tolerance-lowering or revocation actions include a six-month transition/expiration date to allow exporters time to adapt; comments on the adequacy of this transition period may be submitted during the comment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of enforcement methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA has determined it is appropriate based on the underlying safety assessments to take the tolerance actions being proposed in this rulemaking and that adequate enforcement methodology as described in the supporting documents is available to enforce the tolerance expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporting registration review and enforcement-methodology documents in the docket should be consulted to confirm analytical methods and enforcement capability for the proposed tolerance expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority for EPA action (FFDCA §408(e); FIFRA §3(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 408(e) of the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act (FFDCA), 21 U.S.C. 346a(e), authorizes EPA to establish, modify, or revoke tolerances or exemptions from the requirement of a tolerance on its own initiative. Under FIFRA section 3(g), 7 U.S.C. 136a(g), EPA is required to periodically review all registered pesticides and determine if those pesticides continue to meet the standard for registration under FIFRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority citations identify EPA’s statutory bases for initiating tolerance changes during registration review; comments may reference statutory standards (e.g., 'safe' definition) when contesting actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Executive Orders and statutory review exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is exempt from review under Executive Order 12866 because it proposes to establish or modify a pesticide tolerance or a tolerance exemption under FFDCA section 408. Executive Order 14192 does not apply because actions that establish a tolerance under FFDCA section 408 are exempted from review under Executive Order 12866. The action does not impose an information collection burden under the PRA, and EPA certified under the RFA that the action will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities for the reasons stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory review exemptions and certifications (EO12866, PRA, RFA, UMRA, Federalism, Tribal consultation, etc.) apply to tolerance-establishing actions; stakeholders raising procedural or economic concerns should reference relevant statutory review pathways and the docketed analyses described in the rule.
